requirements.requirement: Forward inventory-tagged application logs from node2 to node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: Node2 has an enabled, active rsyslog rule forwarding inventory-tagged messages over TCP to node1. Node1 listens on its managed address, filters node2 inventory messages, and persisted an end-to-end test message at the required path with syslog:adm ownership and mode 0640.

requirements.requirement: Keep log delivery and persisted data working after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart collector state and boot identity were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with a different boot identity, active listener, retained data, and successful delivery of a newly emitted post-recovery inventory message. A message emitted around the disruption was also present after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Keep log delivery working after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node2 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, returned with a different boot identity, retained its forwarding configuration and local data, restored rsyslog and the TCP connection, and delivered a new post-restart inventory message to node1. Node1 retained earlier collected data.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 16.04.7 with kernel 4.4.0-210 before and after execution. The solution used the already-installed rsyslog 8.16.0 package rather than changing the OS, kernel, or logging package.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Inventory-tagged messages flow from node2 to the required persistent file on node1, end-to-end behavior recovered after separate restarts of both systems, and the legacy OS and kernel remained unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and consistent with the fixed boot-identity observations for both nodes.
limitations: End-to-end tests used logger with the inventory tag rather than observing a naturally generated message from a running inventory application; this directly exercises the configured syslog path but leaves the application's own logging integration unobserved.

The fixed lifecycle listening-socket snapshots were empty and therefore do not independently confirm the collector port; direct executor commands repeatedly observed the listener and successful end-to-end delivery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. The retained changes are directly required collector/forwarder configuration and log storage. The temporary configuration move and /tmp validation outputs in cmd-cd58580604cf4a88 supported diagnosis of a pre-existing validation warning; the configuration was restored within the command, and no such temporary files remained after the required reboot. The failed unprivileged attempt in cmd-3f6c3f569159457b does not establish a state change. Final snapshots show no failed services or package damage and only normal reboot-generated temporary directories.
